answer: Draw each identity's three auditors by a public seeded cipher, and count a vouch only when auditor and candidate sit in different graph communities. Clones draw mostly each other: a dense patch of the vouch graph acts like a reef head, where mutual endorsements echo inside the cluster and admit nothing. A farm of n clones draws cross-cluster vouches at rate 1/n, so its expected admission cost grows super-linearly in n while an honest newcomer clears one draw. The failure mode is misread communities, so modularity is recomputed weekly and wrong flags refund the candidate's bond.
